## SC-SCA-CONT-001: StarCraft abilities: bounded affliction and quarantine

Request: Shax t587u (2026-11-25). Catalogue: docs/STARCRAFT_ABILITY_THEOLOGY_MAP.md. Evidence: docs/evidence/starcraft-abilities/abilities.jsonl.

### Invariant
Harm has hard bounds. An affliction can be bounded below by a floor it cannot cross (Plague cannot kill; Job's life is spared), and a contagion centred on one carrier is contained by separating the carrier from the camp, not by healing every neighbour.

Texts: Job 1:12; Job 2:6-7; 1 Cor 10:13; Lev 13:45-46; Num 5:2-3

SC-MAFUBA-001 clauses illustrated: 001B, 001C. Illustration only; SC-MAFUBA-001 is Proposed GOLD, gold_awarded false, not validated by this entry.

### STRONG rows

#### BW-Z05 — Defiler: Plague [STRONG]
- Mechanic (game canon): Units in the area take armour-ignoring damage over time until up to 295 HP is lost or the unit falls to 1-3 HP. Plague cannot kill.
- Counterpart (text): 'He is in your hand; only spare his life.' Job is struck with sores from sole to crown.
- Citation: Job 2:6-7; Job 1:12; 1 Cor 10:13
- Invariant (interpretation): The adversary's affliction is bounded: it can push the body down to a floor but cannot cross into death.
- Residual: Job's floor is set by God's permission (an outside authority bounds the adversary); Plague's floor is a game rule with no permission-giver. The bound is identical in shape; its source is not.
- MAFUBA: 001B: a control barrier function. The attack can drive state toward the boundary h(x) = HP - 1 >= 0 but never across it, which is the robust-CBF shape: a safe set the dynamics cannot leave.
- Sources: bw/Defiler

#### BW-T12 — Science Vessel: Irradiate [STRONG]
- Mechanic (game canon): Damages one biological unit and every biological unit next to it over 25 s. Players answer by moving the irradiated unit away from its group (or burrowing it, for Zerg).
- Counterpart (text): The infectious person lives alone, outside the camp.
- Citation: Lev 13:45-46; Num 5:2-3
- Invariant (interpretation): Contagion centred on one carrier is contained by separating the carrier from the group.
- Residual: As SC2-Z25: impurity versus damage. Here the caster is Terran, so the contagion weapon belongs to the human third faction, not to the invader. Numbers 16:46-48 (Aaron standing between the dead and the living) is a different remedy (an intercessor, not separation) and is not used.
- MAFUBA: 001C: as SC2-Z25.
- Sources: bw/Science Vessel

#### SC2-Z25 — Viper: Parasitic Bomb [STRONG]
- Mechanic (game canon): Attaches a cloud to one enemy air unit that damages it and every enemy air unit near it. Players answer by splitting the target away from the group.
- Counterpart (text): The infectious person lives alone, outside the camp, so the camp is not defiled.
- Citation: Lev 13:45-46; Num 5:2-3
- Invariant (interpretation): Contagion centred on one carrier is contained by separating the carrier from the group.
- Residual: Levitical impurity is ritual contagion, not damage; reading it as harm to neighbours is a structural reading, recorded as such. The carrier in the game is an innocent victim, which fits Leviticus (impurity, not guilt) better than Joshua 7 (Achan's guilt), so Joshua 7 was rejected.
- MAFUBA: 001C: causal containment. Harm propagates along proximity edges; containment cuts the propagation graph by isolating the source node rather than healing every neighbour.
- Sources: sc2/Viper (Legacy of the Void)

### Context rows (not STRONG; not promoted)

#### BW-T11 — Science Vessel: Defensive Matrix [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): Places a temporary barrier on a friendly unit that absorbs a fixed amount of damage.
- Counterpart (text): The hedge God put around Job and all he has.
- Citation: Job 1:10
- Invariant (interpretation): Protection placed by another around one person.
- Residual: Job's hedge is a permission boundary on the adversary, not a damage absorber, and it is removed by permission, not by being used up.
- Sources: bw/Science Vessel

### Grading rule
STRONG needs three or more shared causal features, a text that itself describes the structure, and survival of the recorded disanalogy. Names borrowed from religious vocabulary earn nothing.
